questions: Do your symptoms feel worse at the end of the day or after prolonged use of your eyes?
Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids that comes and goes?
Is there any double vision, especially when you look up?
Have you experienced any recent change in your vision, like blurriness?
Is there any pain or discomfort with eye movement?
Do you have any numbness, weakness, or difficulty with coordination anywhere else in your body?
Have you had any difficulty swallowing, slurred speech, or shortness of breath?
Have you noticed any bulging of your eyes or swelling around them?
Have you had any recent fever, illness, or injury to your head or eye area?
Has anyone in your family had similar eye problems or diseases like myasthenia gravis or thyroid disease?

order_raw:
Based on the history — isolated upward gaze deficit, no fatigability, no ptosis, no pain, no systemic or bulbar symptoms — the critical question is whether this is **restrictive** or **paretic**. Everything flows from that distinction.

1. Forced duction test of the left eye (passive elevation)
2. CT orbits with fine axial and coronal cuts
3. Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4)
4. Anti-AChR antibody and anti-MuSK antibody levels
5. MRI brain and orbits with thin sections through the midbrain
dx: Acute ischaemic infarct of the dorsal paramedian midbrain affecting the rostral interstitial nucleus of the medial longitudinal fasciculus and/or the interstitial nucleus of Cajal (dorsal midbrain syndrome / Parinaud syndrome)
